Photo: AP PHOTO A Lim Kim has pulled away from a crowded pack in most spectacular fashion when she made a hole-in-one on the par-3 16th and posted an eight-under 64 to build a three-shot lead over defending champion Jeeno Thitikul in the CME Group Tour Championship.

She finished with a long two-putt par to reach 15-under 129, the lowest 36-hole score since this tournament moved there in 2013.
 Nelly Korda, in her bid to win the season finale to get into the LPGA Hall of Fame, shot a 67 and still wound up losing ground. She started three shots behind and now is six back on a course that has been relatively soft with wide fairways that allow for low scoring.
 "It gets frustrating because I feel like I have a thought and then I look at my swing and I'm like, 'This is all timing and it's just ...' Yeah, golf is fun sometimes, right?," said the world No.1.
 Nelly Korda is in a tie for 11th after 36 holes in Florida. (AP PHOTO) It certainly felt that way to Kim, the 2020 US Women's Open champion, who delivered one shot that stole the spotlight on a warm, cloudy day. She hit seven-iron from 168 yards that pitched in front of the pin, took one bounced and disappeared.
 Kim followed with a five-foot birdie on the par-5 17th and is halfway home to $US4 million ($A6 million) prize, the richest payoff in women's golf.
 "I needed 155-yard shot, honestly a little strong hit and I make it," Kim said of her ace.
 "A little luck to me, yeah."
 First-round co-leader Karis Davidson, one of four Australians in the field, shot a 70 after her opening 65 to be six off the pace in a tie for 11th.
 Grace Kim (70) is seven under, world No.11 Hannah Green (70) six under and Cassie Porter (76) four over.
 Thitikul was even par on the front nine and falling behind until she made five birdies over the last eight holes for a 67 that puts her in the final group with Kim.
 The 23-year-old has won the CME Group Tour Championship the last two years, famously finishing eagle-birdie last year.
 "I feel like here, the golf course and me are in sync a little bit somehow," the Thai said.
 "Maybe superstitious things, but I feel comfortable to be here."
 The first prize is so big for the LPGA that 24 players in the field have yet to reach $4 million in career earnings. Five of those were bunched together at 11 under, including Japan's Yuri Yoshida (65), who won the BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea during the recent four-week swing through Asia.
 Also four shots behind are South Korea's Ina Yoon (65), Yan Liu (66) of China, American pair Jenny Bae (67) and Auston Kim (67) and England's Charley Hull, who won her first LPGA title at this tournament 10 years ago, when the first prize was a mere $500,000.
 With AAP.
